note: Cases 1-6 have fixtures and are checkable with check.py. Cases 7-9 are judgment cases with no mechanical assertion; a human reads the output.

cases.name: technical-spec-preserves-modality-and-structure
cases.tests: The hard case. Surface tells must go while everything load-bearing survives.
must_fix: 'serves as' -> 'is'
'it is important to note that' cut
em dash after 'operator metadata'
'could potentially' -> one modal
'not just X, it's Y' stated once
'Experts believe' named or cut
'plays a crucial role' replaced with what it does
Title Case heading -> sentence case
must_not_break: MUST, SHOULD, may all survive with the same force
the three bold-lead parameter items stay as a list: this is reference format, not a tell

cases.name: narrative-launch-post-full-slop
cases.tests: Whether the skill restructures rather than word-swapping, and whether it invents numbers to fill the gaps it creates.
must_fix: 'marks a pivotal moment' cut
emoji removed
'At its core' and 'not just X, it's Y' cut
'delving into the landscape', 'showcase', 'harness' cut
tricolon 'faster, cheaper, and more reliable' reduced to what is supported
false range 'everything from X to Y' cut
'Let's dive in', 'Honestly?' cut
challenges-then-outlook formula and uplift ending cut
chatbot residue in the last line cut
must_not_break: no invented proving times, percentages, or benchmark figures: the source has none
'dropped significantly' may stay vague or be flagged as a gap, but must not become a number

cases.name: adr-keeps-rejected-options-and-quotes
cases.tests: Two safeguards that override the pattern list. Pattern 35 says cut invented alternatives; in an ADR the rejected options ARE the content. Quotations are inviolable even when they contain flagged words.
must_fix: 'reducing complexity and highlighting our commitment to operational simplicity' participial editorial cut
must_not_break: the sharding and PGA options must remain with their reasons: deleting them guts the document
Priya's quote must survive verbatim including 'delve', 'testament', and its em dash

cases.name: thin-source-must-not-fabricate
cases.prompt: Humanize this conference recap and make it engaging.
cases.tests: The highest-severity failure mode. The text is deliberately vague and the instruction invites color. There is nothing to add.
must_fix: flat repetitive sentence rhythm
must_not_break: no conference name, city, venue, speaker, talk title, or date may appear
the correct behavior is to improve the rhythm and tell the user the post needs real detail only they have

cases.name: writing-sample-overrides-defaults
cases.prompt: Rewrite the draft to match my writing sample above it.
cases.tests: Safeguard 4. The author writes in fragments and em dashes, which patterns 14 and 31 would normally strip. The sample outranks the pattern list.
must_fix: 'represents a significant advancement', 'leverages cutting-edge', 'seamless', 'robust', 'a wide range of' all cut
output should sound like the sample: short, blunt, first person
must_not_break: the sample's own em dashes and fragments must not be sanded off
matching the sample's fragment style in the rewrite is correct, not a violation
cases.check: manual: check.py will flag em dashes in the output, which is EXPECTED here

cases.name: do-no-harm-on-clean-prose
cases.tests: The null case. The text is already human and already good. The skill must recognize there is little to do rather than demonstrate effort.
must_fix: nothing, or near nothing
must_not_break: Ike, March, 15%, eleven minutes, thirty seconds all survive
no staccato: check scan.py short_sentence_ratio and longest_short_run on the output
the closing reflection is the author's point, not an uplift ending to cut

cases.name: negative-trigger-internal-research
cases.prompt: Summarize this founder interview into a research brief on the company's product and roadmap, so I can decide whether to reach out.
cases.tests: Triggering boundary. This is a drafting request whose output is an input to the requester's own thinking.
cases.expected: The skill does not fire. Output is a dense brief with structure, bolded labels, and tables intact. No voice work.

cases.name: negative-trigger-code-task
cases.prompt: Refactor this Rust function to use a bounded channel and explain the backpressure trade-off.
cases.tests: Over-triggering on any request containing prose. The explanation is technical exposition, not a document with an audience.

cases.name: mixed-register-readme
cases.prompt: Clean up the README for my Rust crate. The intro tells the story of why I built it, then there's an installation section and a config table.
cases.tests: Per-section classification. One document, two rule sets.
cases.expected: Narrative rules on the intro, technical rules from the installation heading down. The config table is untouched.
